item.title: AI Briefing — Sunday, May 17, 2026
item.description: Anthropic is reportedly close to buying Stainless, the four-year-old New York startup whose AI-powered compiler auto-generates production-ready SDKs and MCP servers for OpenAI, Google, Meta, Cloudflare, and Cerebras — meaning Anthropic could soon own the toolchain rivals use to ship their own developer libraries. The deal, first reported May 12, values Stainless at over $300M and would give Anthropic a compounding flywheel over the developer infrastructure layer as MCP adoption surges across the industry. OpenAI announced Friday that co-founder and president Greg Brockman will permanently lead all product strategy, formally merging ChatGPT, the Codex coding agent, and the developer API into a single organization three days before Google I/O 2026 opens on May 19. The goal is a desktop 'super app' that unifies Codex, ChatGPT, and the Atlas browser into one agentic workspace — a direct response to Claude Code's developer momentum and Google's Gemini push, though no firm launch date has been set.

item.title: AI Briefing — Saturday, May 16, 2026
item.description: OpenAI launched a personal finance feature for ChatGPT Pro users in the US on May 15, letting them securely connect accounts from over 12,000 financial institutions through Plaid — including Chase, Fidelity, Schwab, Robinhood, and American Express. Once linked, ChatGPT provides a live dashboard of spending habits, subscriptions, portfolio performance, and upcoming payments, powered by GPT-5.5 Thinking. This marks a significant move by OpenAI to position ChatGPT as a 'super app' interface layer between users and their money, threatening fintech incumbents and raising notable privacy questions. Anthropic launched Claude for Small Business on May 13, a packaged set of 15 ready-to-run agentic workflows, 15 reusable skills, and connectors to QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot, Canva, DocuSign, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack — all installed as a toggle inside Claude Cowork. The product targets the 36 million US small businesses that have largely been left out of the AI boom, handling tasks like payroll planning, month-end close, invoice chasing, and campaign management. Alongside the launch, Anthropic is offering a free AI Fluency course co-developed with PayPal and a 10-city US workshop tour.

item.title: AI Briefing — Friday, May 15, 2026
item.description: On May 14, 2026, OpenAI rolled out Codex inside the ChatGPT mobile app on iOS and Android as a preview available across all plans, including Free and Go tiers. The phone acts as a live control panel — developers can approve agent commands, review diffs, redirect running tasks, and monitor terminal output without returning to their desk. OpenAI also made Remote SSH generally available and added HIPAA-compliant Codex for eligible Enterprise workspaces in the same announcement. Meta launched Incognito Chat with Meta AI on May 13, 2026, a feature for WhatsApp and the Meta AI app that processes conversations in Trusted Execution Environments so that even Meta cannot read them — conversations are not saved and disappear by default when the session ends. The feature is designed for sensitive questions about health, finances, or personal matters, and is rolling out globally over coming months. Unlike competitor 'temporary' modes, Meta claims no server-side access to message content, though security researchers have flagged accountability concerns.

item.title: AI Briefing — Thursday, May 14, 2026
item.description: At the Android Show: I/O Edition on May 13, 2026, Google unveiled Gemini Intelligence — a sweeping suite of agentic AI features that lets Android complete multi-step tasks across apps, auto-fill forms via Gmail context, generate custom widgets from natural language, and browse the web autonomously. Android chief Sameer Samat declared Google is 'transitioning from an operating system to an intelligence system.' Rolling out first to Samsung Galaxy and Pixel this summer, with Google I/O on May 19 expected to bring a new frontier Gemini model announcement. Announced at the Code with Claude 2026 developer conference on May 6, Anthropic introduced 'dreaming' for Claude Managed Agents — a scheduled background process that reviews past agent sessions, extracts patterns, prunes stale memory, and writes refined playbooks before the next session starts. Early adopter Harvey AI reported a 6x jump in task completion rates after implementing it. The feature, invokable via a /dream command or run automatically, does not modify model weights but updates an inspectable external memory layer, making it a major step toward production-grade self-improving agents.

item.title: AI Briefing — Wednesday, May 13, 2026
item.description: At The Android Show: I/O Edition on May 12, Google announced Gemini Intelligence, a suite of agentic AI features that transforms Android from an operating system into what it calls an 'intelligence system.' The update enables Gemini to automate multi-step tasks across apps — booking reservations, building shopping carts, filling complex forms — with user-controlled permissions, rolling out first on Samsung Galaxy and Pixel phones this summer. For AI enthusiasts and developers, Android AppFunctions also debuts, a new API letting app developers expose actions directly to Gemini for high-intent, Gemini-driven user traffic. Anthropic formally launched 'Claude for Legal' on May 12, releasing more than 20 MCP connectors linking Claude to the software law firms run on — including DocuSign, iManage, Relativity, Harvey, and Thomson Reuters' CoCounsel Legal — plus 12 practice-area plugins covering commercial counsel, employment law, and litigation. CoCounsel's next generation is being rebuilt on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, enabling it to plan, select tools, retrieve Westlaw and Practical Law content, and adapt mid-workflow. A recent Claude legal webinar drew over 20,000 registrations, signaling massive demand for AI in legal workflows.

item.title: AI Briefing — Tuesday, May 12, 2026
item.description: AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems sharply raised its IPO price range to $150–$160 per share (up from $115–$125), targeting up to $4.8 billion in proceeds as the offering drew orders more than 20 times the available shares. The Nasdaq listing, expected May 13–14 under ticker CBRS, makes this the largest pure-play AI infrastructure IPO of the year. With a wafer-scale chip 57× larger than Nvidia's H100 and a multi-year OpenAI deal for 750MW of compute, Cerebras is positioning itself as the inference-speed alternative to GPU clusters — directly relevant to anyone watching the AI hardware stack evolve. OpenAI has introduced GPT-Rosalind, a frontier reasoning model purpose-built to accelerate drug discovery, genomics analysis, protein reasoning, and scientific research workflows. This marks a significant push into domain-specific science AI rather than general-purpose assistants, with direct applications for researchers and biotech developers. It signals that the next wave of frontier model launches will be increasingly vertical and task-specific rather than general upgrades.

item.title: AI Briefing — Monday, May 11, 2026
item.description: Anthropic signed an agreement with SpaceX to take all the compute capacity at the Colossus 1 data center, gaining over 300 megawatts and more than 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs within the month to directly expand capacity for Claude Pro and Max subscribers. The company also doubled Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans and removed peak-hours throttling, which matters for any developer hitting Claude Code usage walls. Anthropic even floated partnering with SpaceX on multi-gigawatt orbital AI compute. OpenAI made Workspace Agents generally available to eligible ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces with Enterprise Key Management, letting teams build agents from templates or scratch, share them across a workspace, schedule recurring runs, and trigger them in Slack with custom MCP servers and skills attached. For developers and power users this is the first time ChatGPT's agent layer becomes a managed, governed, schedulable thing rather than a one-off chat session, with version history and analytics built in.

item.title: AI Briefing — Sunday, May 10, 2026
item.description: OpenAI shipped three new audio models on May 7: GPT-Realtime-2 with GPT-5-class reasoning and a 128K context window, GPT-Realtime-Translate covering 70+ input languages into 13 outputs, and a streaming Whisper variant — all in the Realtime API. Translate at $0.034/min and Whisper at $0.017/min undercut most existing voice pipelines, making it newly practical for hobbyists to build live multilingual assistants and home voice agents. Google introduced Gemma 4 in four sizes (E2B, E4B, 26B MoE, 31B Dense) under Apache 2.0, with the 31B model ranking #3 on the open Arena leaderboard. Edge variants ship native audio input, video and image processing, 128K–256K context, and 140+ languages — making it one of the most capable models hobbyists can run on a single workstation or Jetson Orin.

item.title: AI Briefing — Saturday, May 9, 2026
item.description: Google announced Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is now generally available on Vertex AI and the Gemini API, priced at $0.25/1M input and $1.50/1M output tokens with selectable thinking levels (minimal/low/medium/high). It supports text, image, video, audio, and PDF inputs in a 1M token window — making it a practical workhorse for hobbyists building high-volume agent pipelines, routers, and local-to-cloud hybrid setups. ElevenLabs launched Studio Agent inside ElevenCreative — an AI co-editor that drafts videos directly on the timeline from a text prompt, places sound effects frame-accurately, and lets users interrupt and take back control at any moment. For creators and homelabbers experimenting with automated content workflows, this is a notable jump beyond plain TTS into full multimodal editing assistance.

item.title: AI Briefing — Friday, May 8, 2026
item.description: OpenAI rolled out GPT-5.5-Cyber on Thursday to vetted cyber defenders, a more permissive variant of GPT-5.5 trained for vulnerability identification, patch validation, and malware analysis. While defender-focused, it signals how rapidly frontier models are gaining real-world bug-finding capability, with the UK AI Security Institute reporting GPT-5.5 completed a 32-step simulated cyberattack in 2 of 10 runs. Anthropic's latest Claude Code release adds an ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER environment variable for selecting Bedrock tiers (default/flex/priority), smarter /resume PR URL search across GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, improved MCP connector handling, and expanded OpenTelemetry numeric attributes. Useful for developers and homelabbers running Claude Code against AWS Bedrock or self-hosted MCP servers who want better observability and session recovery.

item.title: AI Briefing — Thursday, May 7, 2026
item.description: Nvidia and Corning announced a multiyear partnership to build three new advanced manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas, expanding Corning's US optical connectivity manufacturing capacity tenfold and creating more than 3,000 jobs. The deal gives Nvidia warrants to invest up to $3.2 billion in Corning and supports a phased transition from copper to optical fiber inside AI rack-scale systems. Anthropic unveiled 10 prebuilt agent templates targeting banking, insurance and asset management tasks like pitchbook drafting, KYC screening and month-end close, deployed via Claude Cowork, Claude Code and Managed Agents. The launch debuted Claude Opus 4.7, which Anthropic says scored 64.37% on Vals AI's Finance Agent benchmark, ahead of GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

item.title: AI Briefing — Wednesday, May 6, 2026
item.description: Anthropic signed a five-year deal to spend $200 billion on Google Cloud TPUs and infrastructure, with capacity coming online starting in 2027. The commitment, reported May 5, signals the staggering infrastructure costs of frontier AI and deepens Anthropic's dependence on Google rather than alternative providers. The Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), within the US Commerce Department, announced agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft and xAI to evaluate frontier AI models before public release. The move expands earlier OpenAI and Anthropic agreements and follows White House concerns over Anthropic's powerful Mythos cybersecurity model.

item.title: AI Briefing — Tuesday, May 5, 2026
item.description: The White House is considering an executive order that would give the federal government a formal role in vetting all new AI models before market release, briefing executives from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI on early plans. A working group of tech executives and U.S. officials would design the oversight process, with options including formal government review. The Pentagon finalized AI agreements with OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, Nvidia, SpaceX, and Reflection AI to expand AI use into classified environments for analysis, logistics, and large-scale data processing. Anthropic was excluded after being labeled a supply-chain risk following a contract dispute, a designation it is contesting in court.
